newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rocket, gunfire attacks reported in Corsica towns.
newsitem.headline: Rocket, gunfire attacks reported in Corsica towns.

text.p: A rocket was fired at a law courts building and a volley of gunfire directed against a police station on the French Mediterranean island of Corsica early on Friday but no one was hurt, police said.

The rocket, believed to be an anti-tank weapon, blasted a hole in the building in Bastia in northern Corsica, while the gunshots were fired at a paramilitary police post at Sainte-Marie-Sicche, south of Ajaccio.
Both attacks took place before dawn.
Gendarmes returned fire in the second attack but it was not known if they hit the car from which the shooting had come.

On Thursday a grenade was thrown at a police barracks in the southern Corsican town of Figari causing minor damage but no injuries and a bomb hit a local office of the Renault automaking firm, also causing damage.

No one claimed responsibility for the Thursday and Friday attacks but such violence is common on the resort island where separatist groups have waged a two-decade-long campaign for greater autonomy from mainland France.

The outlawed Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC) Historic Wing has stepped up its campaign since the detention on December 16 of Francois Santoni, head of the Conculta Naziunalista, the FLNC's legal wing.
Santoni faces charges of attempted extortion and arms violations.
The FLNC traditionally carries out attacks on state facilities as well as "punitive" actions against businesses which refuse to pay "revolutionary taxes" to finance its activities.
